c.tagline: Kyushu's castle city — mighty ramparts, spring-fed gardens, and the volcano-fed plains of Mount Aso.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing here (GO, Uber, DiDi) only dispatches licensed, metered taxis rather than private cars, and street/rank taxis are plentiful and all run on the meter.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police; 119 reaches fire and ambulance. English support is limited on local lines, but the 24/7 Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers translation help.

hood_desc: The buzzing core of downtown Kumamoto, a covered arcade packed with izakaya, bars, department stores and the city's best late-night eating; the tram stops right outside at Torichosuji, making it the natural base for first-timers.
The more refined arcade just north of Shimotori, lined with boutiques, coffee roasters, bookshops and stylish restaurants; quieter than its neighbour but still central and full of local character.
The historic heart around Kumamoto Castle and the Josaien 'Sakura no Baba' merchant village, with museums, the Hosokawa Gyobu-tei garden and green ramparts; best for sightseeing and photography.
The area around the Kyushu Shinkansen station and its Amu Plaza mall, a modern, convenient base for travellers arriving by bullet train, a short tram ride from downtown.
A calm residential district southeast of the centre built around the strolling garden of Suizen-ji Jojuen, with leafy streets and a slower, local pace.
lodging: ANA Crowne Plaza Kumamoto New Sky

water.note: Tap water is pristine groundwater and a local point of pride.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 6am to 11pm; taxis are the main option late at night.
transit.pay: Pay the flat tram fare (around ¥180, ~$1.20) in cash or with a contactless credit/debit card; in 2024 Kumamoto's trams and buses began phasing out nationwide IC cards (Suica/ICOCA) in favour of tap-to-pay bank cards.

transit.m: Airport Liner limousine bus to Kumamoto Sakuramachi Bus Terminal & Kumamoto Station, ~50-60 min
Airport shuttle to Higo-Ozu Station, then JR Hohi Line into the city

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; attentive service is standard and already included.
